title: Time Passes · 7
paragraphs: Night after night, summer and winter, the torment of storms and the arrow-straight stillness of fair weather held court undisturbed. Had anyone been listening from the upper rooms of the empty house, all they could have heard was a gigantic chaos, streaked with lightning, rolling and heaving. The winds and the waves played together like the shapeless bulks of leviathans, their foreheads pierced by no light of reason. They piled one on top of another, lunged and plunged in darkness or daylight (for night and day, months and years, ran together without shape) in idiot games, until it seemed the universe itself was fighting and tumbling, alone, in brute confusion and wanton lust, and to no end.

In spring the garden urns, planted by chance with whatever the wind had blown into them, were as bright as ever. Violets came, and daffodils. Yet the calm and brightness of the day were just as strange as the chaos and uproar of the night. There the trees stood, and there the flowers stood, gazing in front of them, gazing upward, yet seeing nothing at all; they had no eyes, and that made them terrible.
